# `jouet read`

- **Usage:** `jouet read [FLAGS] [PATH]`

Read a map of the repository's most important definitions

`--map` prints, for the files that matter most, the line of each of their most important definitions, sized to a token budget, so an agent can find its way around a repository without reading whole files. It is Aider's repo map rebuilt in Rust: tree-sitter finds every definition and reference, files are ranked by personalised PageRank over who refers to whom, and as many top-ranked definitions are shown as fit the budget. Tags are cached by modification time, so a second map of the same tree only re-reads files that changed.

--focus names a file you are working on, or an identifier you care about: what it uses ranks higher, and a focused file's own definitions are left out, as you already have it open. The budget defaults to 1024 tokens with --focus and 8192 without.

Examples:
  jouet read --map
  jouet read --map --focus src/backend/vfox.rs --focus download
  jouet read --map crates/ --budget 2000

## Arguments
- **`[PATH]`** — With --map, the directory to map (default .)

## Flags
- **`--map`** — Print a map of the most important definitions
- **`--budget <TOKENS>`** — The map's size in tokens, estimated at 4 bytes each
- **`--focus <FILE|NAME>`** — A file you are working on, or an identifier you care about. Repeatable
- **`-h --help`** — Print help
